sms.Watch: UshmaLens Heat Watch, {place}: heat stress expected to rise {day}. Drink water often, avoid the sun 12-4 pm, check on elderly neighbours.
sms.Warning: UshmaLens HEAT WARNING, {place} {day}: dangerous heat (HTSI {htsi}). Stay indoors 11 am-4 pm, drink water every 30 min, take ORS if sweating heavily. Emergency: 108
sms.Emergency: UshmaLens HEAT EMERGENCY, {place} {day}: life-threatening heat. Stay in shade or a cool room, never leave children or elderly alone, go to a cooling centre. Heatstroke signs: call 108 now.

description: Human Thermal Stress Index {htsi} ({level}) expected {day} in {place}. Peak WBGT {wbgt} degC; overnight WBGT {night} degC. Estimated excess deaths across the area {excess} (range {excessLow}-{excessHigh}).

public.label: General public
Watch: Drink water regularly even if not thirsty
Avoid direct sun between 12 and 4 pm
Check on elderly neighbours once a day
Warning: Stay indoors from 11 am to 4 pm
Drink water every 30 minutes; use ORS if sweating heavily
Wear light, loose cotton and cover your head outdoors
Emergency: Go to a cooling centre or the coolest room available
Never leave children, elderly or pets in parked vehicles
Confusion, hot dry skin or fainting is heatstroke: call 108 immediately

elderly.label: Elderly and chronically ill
Watch: Keep medicines out of the heat and take them on time
Keep a fan running and a window open for cross-ventilation
Ask someone to check on you daily
Warning: Do not go out between 11 am and 4 pm
Sip water through the day; ask your doctor if you are on a fluid limit
Sponge with cool water if you feel dizzy or weak
Emergency: Move to a cooling centre or the coolest place in the house
Keep a phone within reach and someone informed
Call 108 at the first sign of confusion or fainting

outdoor_workers.label: Outdoor workers
Watch: Drink a glass of water every 20 minutes at work
Take shaded breaks every hour
Watch co-workers for cramps and dizziness
Warning: Shift heavy work to before 11 am or after 4 pm
Rest 15 minutes in shade every hour
Stop work and cool down at any sign of dizziness or nausea
Emergency: No heavy outdoor work between 11 am and 4 pm
Employers must provide shade, water and ORS on site
A collapsed worker needs cooling and 108 immediately

schools.label: Schools
Watch: Move outdoor assembly and games indoors
Ensure drinking water is available in every classroom
Remind parents to send water bottles
Warning: End classes before 11 am or move to morning shift
Cancel outdoor activity entirely
Keep ORS packets and a cool rest room ready
Emergency: Close schools or hold classes online
Do not hold examinations in unventilated halls
Coordinate with the district administration on closure

hospitals.label: Hospitals and PHCs
Watch: Stock ORS, IV fluids and ice packs
Brief emergency staff on heatstroke triage
Check that cold rooms and fans work
Warning: Activate heat-illness triage in emergency departments
Prepare cooling beds (ice, fans, wet sheets)
Expect a surge of {ed} additional emergency visits across the area
Emergency: Declare heat surge protocol; cancel non-urgent procedures
Deploy mobile medical units to hotspots
Report heat-related deaths and admissions daily to the district

power_utility.label: Power utility
Watch: Review peak-load forecast for the coming days
Defer planned maintenance in affected feeders
Warning: Prepare for evening peak demand from fans and coolers
Prioritise uninterrupted supply to hospitals and cooling centres
Emergency: Suspend load-shedding in affected wards
Keep rapid-response crews on standby for transformer failures

municipal.label: Municipal administration
Watch: Alert ward officers and ASHA workers
Check water kiosks and public taps
Pre-position ORS at health centres
Warning: Open cooling centres in priority wards
Run water tankers to slums and markets
Issue advisories to construction sites to shift working hours
Emergency: Open all cooling centres, extend hours into the night
Enforce the 11 am-4 pm outdoor work restriction
Deploy door-to-door checks on elderly people living alone

emergency.signs: Heatstroke signs: very high fever, confusion, no sweating. Do not wait - call now.
